correctness.rationale: At radius one, write the half-edges as (A,At) and (−Bt,B) with t=tan θ. A rotation by 2π/5 modulo the quarter-turn direction convention generates shifts of π/10. For 0≤t≤r/s the four selected facet projections have the signs used in the frozen proof. The strictly positive weights (1,ρ,ρ,1)/2 eliminate the center and give (p+qt)A+(s−rt)B≤2k. AM–GM fixes both half-edge sizes uniquely at equality, and the tight facet normals span the plane, so equality also fixes the center. An independent symbolic check with z=t/s, S=s²=(5+√5)/8 and K=sB verified the weighted coefficients, four contact identities, and exact omitted-facet slack (5−√5)z(1−Sz/r)/(8(p+qsz)(1−rz)), which is nonnegative over the entire closed interval. Therefore the bound is attained, not just an upper envelope; degenerate projection signs at the endpoints do not remove uniqueness. The product-to-sum denominator is minimized only at the two equivalent endpoints and maximized at π/20, giving the claimed area extremes. The θ=0 rectangle has left endpoints (−p,±q), and the other two corners meet the sides incident to the east vertex. The orbit consists of five distinct rectangles, and all other orientations are strictly suboptimal globally. General radius follows by scaling.
residual_risks: Applies only to Euclidean rectangles in a regular pentagon; no inference for odd polygons generally.
